chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding the injuries of the body that there is retaliation (qisas) for them, or the injured party may accept the blood money (diyah) for the injury, and it should be given to him.
ai.seo_question: What are the options for compensation in cases of bodily injury according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi records Imam Ali’s judicial precedent establishing that for bodily injuries, the victim holds the option between exacting proportional retaliation (qisas) or accepting blood money (diyah). It highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence, allowing the injured party to choose the remedy that best serves their interest, whether justice or compensation. This ruling underscores the practical application of Quranic principles of retribution and compensation in early Islamic legal history.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> judged with regards to what was from the injuries of the body, that regarding these is the retaliation, or the injured one can accept the wergild for the injuries, so he should be given it’.
